//: This is a catch all item for antique military uniform tunics that follow a traditional button-up, 4-pocket, wool design.
description: A heavy, full-length wool coat.  Cumbersome, but warm and with deep pockets.

variants.description: An original, or reproduction, example of the Spanish army’s M26 standard service tunic: formed from wool and with pressed wooden buttons.   Olive green in color with yellowish undertones, the jacket possesses two hip and pleated chest pockets, with a rolled collar fitted with brass insignia and a diamond shaped patch on the left breast denoting branch of service.
A royal blue tunic with 4 patch pockets and silver buttons, with a branch badge pinned to the collar: a Silver crown over a shield bearing the letters 'GS'.
A full-length tunic dyed gray-green, fitted with silver buttons and several pockets.  The collar on this example bares a red badge trimmed in silver, with the letters 'GC' superimposed.

description: A soft, somewhat wedge-shaped hat with a flat top and leather trimmings: the headwear of choice of 20th-century military personnel when bullets aren’t imminently flying, and, sometimes, even when they are.

variants.description: This particular example is predominantly khaki, being both piped and tasseled in red.  A bugle-horn, crossed muskets and sword insignia is pinned to the front, identifying the wearer as serving with the pre-1936 or Nationalist Spanish infantry.

This particular example is predominantly khaki, being both piped and tasseled in light blue.  Two crossed silver lances identify the wearer as serving with the pre-1936 or Nationalist Spanish cavalry.

This particular example is predominantly khaki, being both piped and tasseled in black.  A little silver Renault tank is pinned to the front, identifying the wearer as serving with the pre-1936 or Nationalist Spanish tank corps.

This particular example is predominantly khaki, being both piped and tasseled in yellow.  A silver caduceus insignia is pinned to the front, identifying the wearer as serving with the pre-1936 or Nationalist Spanish medical corps.

This particular example is predominantly khaki, being both piped and tasseled in red.  Golden crossed muskets, halberd and crossbow identify the wearer as serving with the Nationalist Spanish Foreign Legion.  Bad news.
This particular example is predominantly khaki, being piped in red.  A small red star is pinned to the front, identifying the wearer as a fighter of the Spanish Republican government.

This particular example is made from a base layer of red, crossed diagonally on either side with black, marking the wearer as a member of the anarchist movement in Spanish Republican forces.  Wearing it has an equal chance of either attracting señoritas, or bullets.

This particular example is predominantly royal blue, being both piped and tasseled in white.  A silver crown over a shield bearing the letters 'GS' identify the wearer as serving with the Spanish Assault Guards.

This particular example is predominantly gray-green, being both piped and tasseled in red.  A broad red band encircling the bottom and an accompanying silver-trimmed red badge superimposed with the letters 'GC' identify the wearer as serving with the Spanish civil guard.
